candidates.reaction_description: Proton transfer: the N9 amidate lone pair takes an H from N6+. The N6–H bond electrons stay on N6, neutralising it. Both nitrogens end up as neutral NH, giving the urea. The step is atom-balanced and the net charge stays at 0.

output.llm_reasoning: The zwitterionic adduct needs one proton moved from the anilinium N6 (NH2+) to the amidate N9 (N-) to give the neutral urea. The current state holds only this single species, so no external acid or base shuttle is available. The transfer is therefore drawn as an intramolecular N-to-N proton shift. In practice it is mediated by solvent or a second amine molecule, but the net outcome is the same: the neutral target urea, with atoms and charge balanced.
